title: Brunies recordings, Jules Gala and an evening in Biloxi
summary: Allen asks about the Brunies Brothers record and Rose recalls hearing Abbie Brunies' band in Biloxi with Wiggs and Raymond Burke; both note that tastes change over time.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: But before we get too far afield into all the different sessions and what's left today, were you involved in any way with the Brunius Brothers recording or not? No. Nothing to do with it? Not at all. I was just curious, I was listening to that yesterday. It struck me that compared to most clarinet players today, Jules Gala is.
Yeah, he's better than most of them around today.
Sure. I believe, didn't you go out with us to Biloxi one night with Wiggs and Raymond Burke?
To hear the Brunies band, Abbey Brunies band. I enjoyed that night very much and I was very much impressed by the music.

Well it's funny when you go back and listen to things, you reevaluate them. Oh yeah. And I was interviewing Bill Russell last night and he was talking about the masters that he rejected years ago, so I'm great now.
Oh sure. Well, of course your criteria change and the availability of the quality changes substantially, and of course we just don't have any more like we used to have to work with.
